title: Gradient Like Vector Fields and Morse Trajectories

items.title: The Riemannian gradient is the metric dual of the differential
items.strategy: For a Riemannian metric g and f:M→R, define grad_g f as the unique smooth vector field satisfying g(grad_g f,Y)=df(Y) for every smooth vector field Y. Record the pointwise musical-isomorphism construction and its smoothness in a local frame.

items.title: The Riemannian gradient vanishes exactly at the critical points
items.strategy: Use positive-definiteness of g to identify grad_g f(x)=0 with df_x=0, then invoke the established critical-point definition. This is the sign-free bridge used by the energy identity.

items.title: Negative-gradient trajectories of a Morse function
items.strategy: For a Morse function f and metric g, define a negative-gradient trajectory to be an integral curve γ of −grad_g f on its maximal interval; reserve a full trajectory for one with domain R. This fixes the descending sign before stable and unstable conventions are introduced.

items.title: A negative-gradient trajectory satisfies the energy identity
items.strategy: Differentiate f∘γ and use γ˙=−grad_g f to obtain d(f∘γ)/dt=−||grad_g f||_g². State the identity on the maximal interval, without assuming compactness or completeness.

items.title: Nonconstant negative-gradient trajectories strictly decrease the function
items.strategy: Combine the energy identity with the gradient-zero/critical-point equivalence and uniqueness of integral curves: a trajectory meeting a critical point is constant, so every nonconstant trajectory has strictly negative derivative everywhere.

items.title: Downward gradient-like vector fields for a Morse function
items.strategy: Define X to be downward gradient-like for f when df(X)<0 away from Crit(f), and, in Morse coordinates f=f(p)−|u|²+|v|² near every critical point, X=2u·∂u−2v·∂v, the negative Euclidean gradient. The exact local model—not merely descent—is part of the definition.

items.title: Every Morse function admits a complete downward gradient-like field on a closed manifold
items.strategy: Choose disjoint Morse-coordinate neighborhoods, prescribe the exact negative linear model on smaller neighborhoods, and patch it to a strictly descending field away from Crit(f) with cutoffs. Compactness of the closed manifold then makes the resulting smooth field complete; the construction never substitutes an arbitrary descending field at a critical point.

items.title: Precompact trajectory tails have nonempty compact connected flow-invariant limit sets
items.strategy: For a full trajectory whose positive or negative tail has compact closure, define its tail limit set as the nested intersection of closed tail closures. Use compactness for nonemptiness and connectedness of each tail closure, then continuity of the flow for invariance. Keep this topological lemma separate from the energy argument.

items.title: Every precompact end-limit point of a negative-gradient trajectory is critical
items.strategy: On either flow-invariant tail limit set, f is constant because f∘γ is monotone and has a finite limiting value. The energy identity then rules out a noncritical point on that set, since its short orbit segment would lower f strictly while remaining in the same limit set.

items.title: A negative-gradient trajectory on a compact Morse manifold has single critical alpha and omega limits
items.strategy: Use completeness on the compact manifold and the tail-limit lemma. The critical-point lemma places each connected limit set in the finite discrete critical set, hence makes it one point. Record α(γ) for t→−∞ and ω(γ) for t→+∞ explicitly.

items.title: A Morse trajectory from one critical point to another
items.strategy: For a complete negative-gradient trajectory γ of a Morse function, define γ to run from p to q when it is nonconstant and α(γ)=p and ω(γ)=q. On compact manifolds the preceding lemma supplies these endpoints; in noncompact settings they are an explicit hypothesis.

items.title: Morse trajectories have a positive energy drop
items.strategy: Integrate the energy identity from −T to T and pass to the prescribed critical endpoints. For a nonconstant trajectory from p to q, obtain f(p)−f(q)=∫||grad_g f||²dt>0.

items.title: Stable and unstable sets of a critical point
items.strategy: For the complete descending flow Φ of a downward gradient-like field, define Wˢ(p)={x:Φ_t(x)→p as t→+∞} and Wᵘ(p)={x:Φ_t(x)→p as t→−∞}. State the descending-flow convention beside the definition so the index dimensions are not reversed.

items.title: Local stable and unstable manifolds at a Morse critical point
items.strategy: Use the required standard negative linear model in Morse coordinates. Its local unstable disk is {v=0} of dimension index(p), and its local stable disk is {u=0} of dimension n−index(p); state their tangent spaces as the negative and positive Hessian eigenspaces. This is only a local disk theorem.

items.title: Global stable and unstable manifolds are immersed Euclidean spaces
items.strategy: Exhaust each global stable or unstable set by images of its local disk under the complete flow. Flow maps transport the local immersed manifold charts and their compatible inclusions yield Wᵘ(p)≅R^index(p) and Wˢ(p)≅R^(n−index(p)) as immersed submanifolds. Do not upgrade immersed to embedded.

items.title: Stable and unstable manifolds are flow invariant
items.strategy: Apply the flow group law to the defining limits: time-translation of a point with limit p has the same limit. Record invariance for every fixed flow time, including the local-to-global use in the next page.

items.title: A downward gradient flow has no nonconstant periodic or recurrent orbit
items.strategy: Strict decrease of f along every nonconstant orbit contradicts periodic return. For recurrence, take a return sequence and continuity of f to contradict its strictly decreasing values; retain constant critical orbits as the only exception.

items.title: Proper smooth functions and compact Morse slabs
items.strategy: Define a continuous map to be proper when inverse images of compact sets are compact, and call f⁻¹([a,b]) a compact Morse slab when it is compact. This supplies the noncompact compactness hypothesis explicitly rather than importing a hidden properness convention.

items.title: Proper Morse slabs prevent finite-time escape of connecting trajectories
items.strategy: If a maximal negative-gradient trajectory has image contained in a compact slab f⁻¹([a,b]), use the ODE continuation alternative to extend it past either finite endpoint. The energy identity verifies the required trapping whenever the trajectory is known to connect prescribed endpoint levels inside that slab; no blanket completeness claim is made on a noncompact manifold.

items.title: Completeness of a gradient flow is an extra hypothesis on a noncompact manifold
items.strategy: Separate the compact-manifold completeness theorem from noncompact use: a gradient or gradient-like field need not be complete without a trapping/properness argument. Point to the explicit counterexample on the companion page.

title: Gradient Like Vector Fields and Morse Trajectories — Examples

items.title: Negative-gradient lines for a quadratic Morse function
items.strategy: For f(u,v)=−|u|²+|v|² with the Euclidean metric, solve u˙=2u and v˙=−2v. Identify the local unstable and stable coordinate disks and check the energy identity directly.

items.title: Meridian trajectories for height on the sphere
items.strategy: For the round sphere and f(x,y,z)=z, compute the negative-gradient field and identify the nonconstant meridians from the north pole to the south pole. Explain that this is a one-parameter family before quotienting by time translation, not a Morse–Smale assertion.

items.title: Gradient flow for a Morse function on the flat torus
items.strategy: Use f(θ,φ)=cos θ+cos φ on the flat torus, list its four critical points and indices, and solve the separated negative-gradient equations. Exhibit the coordinate-circle separatrices and the remaining one-parameter family from the maximum to the minimum.

items.title: Using the positive gradient reverses the stable and unstable dimensions
items.strategy: Reuse the quadratic Morse model but evolve by +grad f. The u and v exponentials interchange the forward and backward limiting coordinate spaces, showing why the descending-sign convention cannot be left implicit.

items.title: A gradient flow on a noncompact manifold can be incomplete
items.strategy: On R with its Euclidean metric take f(x)=−x³/3, so −grad f=x²∂x and x(t)=x₀/(1−x₀t) blows up at finite positive time for x₀>0. State that the example witnesses incompleteness only; it is not offered as a Morse-function example.
